clue.text: Fruit in shapeless mass page brought forward

indicators.note: brought forward says the page letter is shifted from the back of the word to its front

parts.note: a lump is a shapeless mass

explanation.surface: Some fruit has gone squashy and sits on the page of a recipe book as a formless blob.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a stone fruit, so the general word fruit covers it as an example.

clue.text: Female organised church in the country

parts.note: to run something is to organise it, so organised gives ran
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A woman arranged church affairs out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal but is a plain synonym, RAN; 'the country' is the definition, not the rural countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: France is a nation of western Europe, an example of a country.

clue.text: Marriage possibly over in US city

parts.note: matrimony is one example of a sacrament, hence the 'possibly'
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A wedding is perhaps finished somewhere in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the capital of California, an example of an American city.

clue.text: Pound to dine in revolutionary inn

indicators.note: in places the dining word inside the turned-round inn word
revolutionary means turning round, so the inn word is read backwards

parts.note: a pub is an inn
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone thumps the table as they sit down for a meal in a radical public house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like politics, but it signals turning the inn word round; the dining word then sits just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat someone up is to pound them with blows, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Thus doctor hugs US brother in hat

parts.note: so means thus

indicators.note: hugs means the doctor's letters wrap around the brother word

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
Brer is the Southern US dialect form of brother, as in Brer Rabbit

explanation.surface: A doctor embraces an American brother who is wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat, so it is one kind of headwear.

clue.text: Fellows given superior list of options

parts.note: fellows are men
U stands for upper-class, hence superior

explanation.surface: Members of a college are offered a better list of choices.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu sets out the dishes or computer commands one may choose between.

clue.text: American agents sound sheepish eating dry doughy stuff

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

indicators.note: eating means the sheep's cry swallows the dry letters

parts.note: baa is the bleat a sheep makes
TT means teetotal, so dry

explanation.surface: US spies bleat awkwardly while chewing something dry and stodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound sheepish' suggests embarrassment but means make a sheep's cry; 'dry' is the teetotal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciabatta is an Italian bread made from a wet, open dough.

clue.text: Uncle is lowly man with no money ending in gutter

parts.note: a pawn is the lowliest chess man
broke means penniless

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of gutter

explanation.surface: A relative is a poor wretch, penniless and finishing up in the gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old slang for a pawnbroker, the man who lends money on pledged goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle is long-standing slang for a moneylender who takes goods in pledge.

clue.text: Retired WI batsman eats very little grub

indicators.note: eats means the batsman's name takes the very letter inside it

parts.note: Brian Lara is a retired West Indies batsman

explanation.surface: A cricketer from the West Indies, now retired, has very little to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very little' reads as one phrase, but 'very' gives V and 'little grub' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the young wormlike stage of an insect, which is what a grub is.

clue.text: English drunkard, Heather, collected items of mysterious nature

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
Erica is the botanical genus of heather

explanation.surface: An English boozer called Heather amassed a collection of strange curiosities.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but here it is the plant whose Latin genus is Erica.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure things understood only by a few initiates.

clue.text: A group of soldiers housed in brand-new tower

indicators.note: housed in means these letters are lodged inside the brand-new word

parts.note: in mint condition means brand-new
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: A troop is billeted in a freshly built tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Our good Parisian backing British member of royal family

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the words before it come after the British letter

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A Frenchman praises a royal and supports Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bourbons were the royal house of France and Spain, so one of them is a royal.

clue.text: Best people yell when leader is got rid of

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: a scream is a yell

explanation.surface: The elite shout when their head is ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of society is its finest members, an idiom from the richest part of milk.

clue.text: Old male caught in embrace brings dishonour

indicators.note: caught in means the old male letters are trapped inside the embrace word

parts.note: to embrace is to comprise or include

explanation.surface: An elderly man found in a clinch is disgraced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embrace' looks like a hug but means include, COMPRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise someone is to expose them to disgrace or suspicion, a verb sense of dishonouring.

clue.text: Quiet person taking things easy, keeping near church member

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: keeping means the resting person holds the near word inside

parts.note: a rester is someone resting
by means near, as in standing by

explanation.surface: A quiet loafer stays close to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyter is an elder or priest in certain churches, so an officer among its members.

clue.text: Something on meal table, a crude base that's rickety

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and unsound, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A crude, wobbly base is something on the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rickety' shuffles A CRUDE BASE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread sauce is a British accompaniment made from milk and breadcrumbs, served with roast chicken or turkey.

clue.text: Becoming popular again? That wouldn't affect Abba

definitions.meaning: a return to fashion or success after a period away
the name Abba reads the same both ways, so turning it round does nothing to it

explanation.surface: A wistful note on the Swedish pop group's revival, which apparently changes nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'coming back' literally as reversing a word: Abba is a palindrome, so it survives reversal unchanged. Abba did in fact reunite in 2021.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeback is a return to former popularity, so a group staging one is regaining fans.

clue.text: Legal stitch-up in which you suppose some might get jumpy?

definitions.meaning: an unofficial tribunal that ignores justice and fixes its verdict in advance

definitions.text: in which you suppose some might get jumpy?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a ... full of hopping marsupials, which would certainly be jumpy

explanation.surface: A rigged trial where the accused might understandably feel nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpy' looks like nervousness but points to marsupials that hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court is a mock trial that disregards proper legal process.

clue.text: A firm has us twitching — is it good if we can hear?

definitions.text: is it good if we can hear?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A company worries that our nervous fidgeting matters to whether we can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitching' looks like an anagram signal for 'us', but it is the synonym TIC; 'us' stands as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic describes sound and hearing, as in the acoustics of a hall being good or bad.

clue.text: Bitter scorn — our aunt's beginning to be horrible

indicators.note: horrible suggests a mess, so the gathered letters are jumbled
beginning takes just the first letter of aunt's

explanation.surface: A sour put-down from our aunt starts to turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges SCORN, OUR and the A from 'aunt's beginning'; 'to be' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous means full of deep-seated resentment, which is bitterness.

clue.text: Catholic head of school with a set of beliefs exuding love

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of school
exuding means giving off, so the love letter leaves the creed word

parts.note: a credo is a set of beliefs, a creed
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A Catholic headteacher with firm convictions radiates warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' looks like a faith but is a loose synonym for holy; CREDO loses O.
explanation.definitionFit: In the religious sense both words mean consecrated and of the Church, giving a sense of holy.

clue.text: Cleric I had written about, footballing cheat

indicators.note: written about means the letters are set down turned around, back to front

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A vicar admits he wrote about a player who fakes fouls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' signals the whole of cleric plus I'd turned back to front, giving REVID reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: In football slang a diver is a player who falls theatrically to win a free kick or penalty.

clue.text: Mist, very limited, above a stream

indicators.note: above places the first letter over the rest in this down answer
limited says only the first letter of very is kept

parts.note: to pour is to stream

explanation.surface: A slight mist hangs over a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour is moisture suspended in the air, which is what a mist consists of.

clue.text: Fuss in horses' accommodation — lead the horses out to these?

definitions.text: lead the horses out to these?

indicators.note: in places the fuss word inside the stabling word

parts.note: mews were originally stables round a yard
ado means fuss

explanation.surface: A commotion in the stables, so it's time to take the horses out to graze.
explanation.walkthrough: MEWS today means smart London housing converted from stables; originally they housed horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadows are grassy fields, the sort of pasture horses are turned out onto.

clue.text: Sign of more than one female losing head

indicators.note: losing head drops the first letter of the plural word

parts.note: the plural of woman

explanation.surface: A mark of several women having lost their composure.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Trick needed to cross slope — something climber uses

indicators.note: to cross means the trick word stretches over the slope word, around it

parts.note: a con is a trick
a ramp is a slope

explanation.surface: A dodge is needed to get across a steep bank, a mountaineer's ploy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked metal frame fixed to a boot for gripping ice.

clue.text: Do for one!

parts.note: do reads as a verb or a party, but it is the first syllable of the sol-fa scale, an example of a musical sound

explanation.surface: An exclamation, as if urging a single person to get something done.
explanation.walkthrough: Do (doh) is the first note of the sol-fa scale; 'for one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Do is one of the named tones of the scale, so it is an example of a musical tone.

clue.text: See rhino moving around lake, where land and water meet

indicators.note: moving around means the letters shift into a different arrangement

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Watch a rhinoceros wandering round a lake at the water's edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoreline is the boundary line of a coast or bank, the edge between ground and sea.

clue.text: See 17
